sources.entry: OpenRemote - IoT Asset management, Flow Rules and WHEN-THEN rules, Data visualization, Edge Gateway. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Java

summary.one_liner: OpenRemote Core is an open source IoT platform for device management, asset modelling, automation rules, data analytics and dashboards, written in Java.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a platform for building IoT device management solutions, covering device management and auto provisioning, customizable asset types, and automation through when-then, flow, JavaScript and Groovy rules. It lists connectivity through several protocol agents and manager APIs (MQTT broker, HTTP/REST, WebSocket), plus multi-tenancy via realms and user and role management. It also mentions an edge gateway, front-end UI web components and consoles, and an Insights dashboard builder for data visualization. Attribute history is kept indefinitely by default, with an environment variable (OR_DATA_POINTS_MAX_AGE_WEEKS) to purge older data. Persistence uses PostgreSQL in a Docker volume.
use_cases: Automate devices with when-then or flow rules
Connect devices over MQTT, HTTP/REST or WebSocket
Build dashboards to visualize sensor data
Run a multi-tenant smart city or building platform
Deploy an edge gateway for IoT sites
how_to_run: Download the OpenRemote Stack docker compose file from the README link
Open the Manager UI in a browser and accept the self-signed certificate
Optionally set OR_HOSTNAME=<host> when accessing from a VM or another machine
notable: Automation via when-then, flow, JavaScript and Groovy rules
Multi-tenancy through realms with user and role management
Edge gateway and Insights dashboard builder
Docker images for amd64 and arm64
caveats: Default access uses a self-signed certificate and the README's default URL must be changed via OR_HOSTNAME for VM or remote access
Development setup requires the Developer Guide and a Gradle/Java toolchain
